claims.text: DSS borrows the coarse-to-fine idea from multigrid and temporal reconstruction, not any graphics implementation.
claims.why: No code references multigrid or temporal reconstruction; claim is conceptual.

claims.text: Version zero deliberately contains no learned interpolation, hidden-state transport, differentiable program space, or diffeomorphic claim
claims.why: No code in this chunk implements or mentions those features; claim is about absence.

claims.text: source files form leaves in a deterministic repository/directory hierarchy
claims.why: build_forest_hierarchy creates hierarchy with file nodes as leaves; FILE_NODE_KINDS defines source files.

claims.text: seed relevance is restricted upwards and prolonged through a bounded number of high-scoring branches
claims.why: restrict_scores restricts scores upwards (to ancestors). Prolongation is defined but its bounded traversal is not implemented in this chunk.

claims.text: each evidence relation diffuses in its own channel
claims.why: No evidence relation or diffusion code in this chunk.

claims.text: previous scores may be carried by exact IDs or explicit rename evidence
claims.why: No score carry or rename evidence code in this chunk.

claims.text: the fused ranking is packed into a token budget
claims.why: No packing or token budget code in this chunk.

claims.text: every input and decision is represented by a content-addressed receipt.
claims.why: No receipt code in this chunk.

claims.text: The module is dependency-free and read-only.
claims.why: Imports only from standard library and .forest module; no writes or side effects observed.

claims.text: It selects context; it never changes source code and never treats a relevance score as a fitness signal.
claims.why: No mutation of source code; scores are used for selection only.

claims.text: document is here because the defect this feature exists to fix is a SELECTION defect: a task specified entirely in a 3592-line markdown architecture document got a context plan of three TypeScript files, because the specification was not a node the selector could see. A document that is indexed but unselectable fixes nothing.
claims.why: Historical motivation; no code verifies this.

claims.text: type and field are DELIBERATELY ABSENT, and adding them is not a completion of this set, it is a defect.
A document has bytes on disk; a type node is a derived assertion about a region of a file that is already a node.
claims.why: Claim about forest node semantics; not verifiable in this chunk.

claims.text: Admit it here and it becomes a hierarchy leaf, a legal seed and a budget candidate -- at which point _estimated_tokens falls through to its loc * 8 fallback and invents a token cost for something no reader can read, while the file that actually holds the declaration may be dropped for lack of budget.
claims.why: Refers to _estimated_tokens and budget logic not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Type evidence RE-SCORES file nodes; it is never itself the thing shipped to a model. forest.py's module docstring carries the full argument, including the measured 2-hop blow-up that keeps these relations out of diffusion as well (see _relation_adjacencies).
claims.why: Refers to code in forest.py not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Input keys are authoritative Forest node IDs. Output keys are hierarchy IDs. Unknown source IDs are rejected so a typo cannot silently alter the branch selection.
claims.why: restrict_scores uses files dict from file_node_map(); raises KeyError for unknown IDs.

observations.what: build_forest_hierarchy raises ValueError if two forest node IDs map to same canonical path.
restrict_scores raises KeyError for unknown forest file IDs.
Prolongation dataclass is defined but incomplete in this chunk; only file_scores field visible.
FILE_NODE_KINDS includes 'source_file', 'file', and 'document'; excludes 'type' and 'field' as documented.
